name: Tumulung Sisaala
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Rowland, Ronald & Muriel Rowland 1965, Collected field reports on the phonology of Sisala (IAS, Legon); also Funke 1922, Die Isala-Sprache im Westsudan (grammar sketch)
earlier_scan.note: Dedicated phonology (Rowland & Rowland 1965) exists but no online copy found; Webonary Sisaali dictionary 403-blocked

sources.citation: Jambadu, Jacob Bayaamogo. 2024. Compounding in Sɩsaalɩ. MPhil thesis, University of Education, Winneba.
sources.note: Kpatoli dialect; states Sisaali is a tone language; stress discussed only for English compound-stress theory.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sisaala language' (accessed 2026-09-17); Glottolog 5.x languoid page tumu1242.
sources.note: Wikipedia: dialect geography only, no phonology; Glottolog page: names, ISO code, no additional descriptive refs beyond the four in WORLD_TARGETS.

sources.citation: Mustapha, Nuuratu. 2018. The morpho-syntax of the noun phrase in Sɩsaalɩ. MPhil thesis, University of Ghana, Legon.
sources.note: Kpatolie (south-western) dialect. Sec. 1.2.3: 9 phonemic vowels, 24 consonants, ATR harmony, 'Sɩsaalɩ is a tonal language and tone plays important roles in the grammar and lexical inventory'; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Bushira, Gariba. 2017. Some word formation processes in Sɩsaalɩ. MPhil thesis, University of Education, Winneba.
sources.note: Data explicitly from the Tumuluŋ dialect. p. 2: lexical and grammatical tone minimal pairs, 'Hence, Sɩsaalɩ can be said to be a tone language'; sec. 2.5 reviews consonants, vowels, syllable types (every syllable carries a tone). The word 'stress' occurs only in a remark on English clusters; silent on Sisaali stress.

sources.citation: Dumah, Irene Basimaga. 2017. Question markers in Sɩsaalɩ. MPhil thesis, University of Education, Winneba.
sources.note: Paasaal dialect data; no phonology chapter; 'stress' appears only in general remarks on prosodic focus marking in other languages.

sources.citation: Moran, Steven. 2009 (ms., April 10). A Grammar of Isaalo, Sisaala Western [ssl]. University of Washington, work in progress.
sources.note: west2465. Phonology chapter with sec. 2.4 Tone (two tones, lexical and grammatical); no stress/accent section or statement.

sources.citation: Moran, Steven Paul. 2006. A grammatical sketch of Isaalo (Western Sisaala). MA thesis, Eastern Michigan University (DigitalCommons@EMU theses/73).
sources.note: WESTERN Sisaala (west2465). Sec. 4.5 'Suprasegmentals' (pp. 87-96) covers tone (register H/L, no mid) and intonation only; 'accent' occurs only in the literature discussion of tonal vs accentual systems; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Bawine, Edwin Tommuah (tr.). 1977. Sisaala [Genesis 1-3 selections]. Tamale: Ghana Institute of Linguistics.

Blass, Regina (ed.). 1975. Sisaala-English, English-Sisaala Dictionary. Tamale: Institute of Linguistics (Ghana). Front matter 'Notes on the Use of the Dictionary' pp. viii-x and 'Grammatical Notes' pp. xiii-xv (Rosetta Project excerpts).
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Tone' (p. ix): 'Tone is not marked in Isaaliŋ orthography'; the dictionary marks higher tone with acute and lower tone with grave where minimal pairs exist. Nothing about stress. Glottolog files this dictionary under tumu1242; Rosetta/Wikipedia tag it ssl (Western Sisaala).

sources.citation: Rowland, Ron. 1966. Sissala noun groups. Journal of West African Languages 3(1): 23-28.
sources.note: Sec. 2 'The phonemes' (p. 24) lists 10 vowels, 24 consonants and 'four tones: high, low, rising and falling' with their diacritics; nothing on stress or accent. Dialect: Issala of Nabugajan, 15 miles SW of Tumu.

sources.citation: Naden, Tony. 1988. The Gur languages. In M. E. Kropp Dakubu (ed.), The Languages of Ghana, 12-49. London: Kegan Paul International for the International African Institute.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Survey chapter that summarises the phonology of the Gur languages of Ghana including Sisaala (tone, syllable, possibly stress); cited by all the Sisaali theses for dialect classification.

sources.citation: Frempong, Margrit & Caleb Batong. 2021. Sisaali Dictionary. Tamale: GILLBT (Webonary edition).

sources.note: Glottolog's newest source for tumu1242 (371 pp.); GILLBT/Webonary dictionaries carry an introduction on the sound system, tone and orthography that may state whether stress plays any role.

sources.citation: Luri, Moses Dramani. 2011. Aspects of Sɩsaalɩ Phonology. MA thesis, University of Ghana, Legon.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Native-speaker phonology of Sisaali covering the seven dialects including Tumuluŋ (syllable structure, inventories per Bushira 2017 pp. 30-31); the most likely modern statement on prosody. Not indexed in UGSpace; may exist only in the Linguistics Department library.

sources.citation: Toupin, Mike. 1995. The phonology of Sisaale-Pasaale (Collected Language Notes 22). Legon: Institute of African Studies.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Modern SIL phonology of the sibling Paasaal variety (paas1238); the closest full phonological description of any Sisaala variety and the source the Ghanaian theses rely on for inventories; would say whether stress is described for Sisaala at all.
